subject: MAP: escrow plan for evaluation assets + restricted test cases
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marta Soto <marta@hightower.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 14:06:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: escrow plan for evaluation assets + restricted test cases

Hi Marta —

Following our call this morning, attached is a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) focused on the dataset handoff and restricted test cases you requested. High-level goals:

- Provide Hightower access to a representative eval kit (prompt packs + test cases) under a short-term, auditable escrow so you can run regressions and latency/cost profiling.
- Keep dataset usage restricted to evaluation only (no redistribution, no external benchmarking publications without prior consent).
- Close commercial terms and finalize SOW by Jan 12 to align with your Jan 15 renewal.

What I attached: eval-manifest-v1.csv (file manifest with sample counts) and MAP-milestones.pdf (timeline + gating conditions).

Proposed milestones (summary):
1) Dec 20 — Legal agrees to usage constraints and escrow delivery mechanism (S3 pre-signed + one-time token).
2) Dec 22 — Redlines exchanged and DocuSign package created.
3) Dec 28 — Finalized access granted; 14-day evaluation window begins.
4) Jan 10 — Results review + pricing/commit decision.

Key constraints we need on your side (so our legal & security teams are comfortable):
- Access limited to named evaluators (Nate Chong, Marta Soto).
- No redistribution; no publishing of test case contents.
- Data must be deleted at end of evaluation window; audit logs to be provided.

If this timeline works, I’ll ask legal to produce a short data-use addendum and a DocuSign to capture acceptance. Please confirm who from Hightower will sign.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

---------------------------------------------------------------
From: Marta Soto <marta@hightower.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Nate Chong <nate@hightower.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP: escrow plan for evaluation assets + restricted test cases

Thanks Alex — this looks reasonable and we appreciate the clarity on milestones. A few notes from our side:

- Legal wants an escrow mechanism that provides an auditable chain (verifiable download events + single-use links).
- We need minimal redaction on PII fields in the testcases; our security team requires examples that are representative but not production-sensitive.
- Signing authority: Legal can countersign (Hightower Legal <legal@hightower.ai>), but business signoff will be by me.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will host the files in a locked S3 bucket with expiring presigned URLs, or will we receive a physical transfer? Also confirm whether KMS keys remain under Redwood control or if Hightower can bring its own key for the eval window.

—Marta
Director of Data Platforms, Hightower Analytics

---------------------------------------------------------------
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marta Soto <marta@hightower.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: escrow plan for evaluation assets + restricted test cases

Hi Marta — great questions. Short answers:

- Delivery mechanism: we’ll host the eval kit in a locked, private S3 bucket in us-west-2 and issue presigned GET links with a 72-hour TTL per user. Access requires a one-time access token tied to the user’s email. We’ll log every download and provide the audit CSV at the end of the evaluation.
- KMS: by default Redwood will hold the master key; however, for Dedicated/Private pilots we can support a customer-managed KMS. For this short evaluation we propose Redwood-managed KMS but with envelope encryption and strict IAM policies limiting access to a named service principal.
- PII/redaction: we can produce a redacted variant of the testcases. I’ve noted this in MAP-milestones.pdf as a gating condition before download.

I’ve also prepared a DocuSign preview for the data-use addendum (link below) and will work with our legal to incorporate the audit-log requirement.

DocuSign (preview): https://docusign.com/preview/abc123-eval-escrow

If Hightower is comfortable with Redwood-managed KMS for the 14-day window, we’ll proceed with the DocuSign + presigned link flow (Dec 22 delivery).

Best,
Alex

---------------------------------------------------------------
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: escrow plan for evaluation assets + restricted test cases

Looping in Ben for the KMS/audit specifics — Ben, can you confirm the audit CSV fields we can provide and the TTL enforcement for presigned URLs? Also, if we redact PII, what is our expected turnaround for generating the redacted package?

-Lauren
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

---------------------------------------------------------------
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 12:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: escrow plan for evaluation assets + restricted test cases

Lauren / Alex —

We can provide the following for the eval window:
- Audit CSV with columns: user_email, object_key, presigned_link_id, access_timestamp_utc, ip_address, action (GET), bytes_transferred.
- Presigned URLs will auto-expire at TTL (72 hours) and we can rotate the links daily if needed.
- Redaction: we can produce a redacted package within 48 business hours from receiving the redaction spec (list of fields/columns to scrub).
- KMS: Redwood-managed CMKs only for this eval. If Hightower opts for BYOK later, we’ll coordinate a key wrap handover in the Dedicated onboarding flow.

I’ll attach a short checklist to make handoff smoother and will add the audit sample CSV to the shared doc.

—Ben
Security Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redlines_hightower_v1.docx (placeholder for legal redlines)

---------------------------------------------------------------
From: Marta Soto <marta@hightower.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Dec 2026 17:35:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP: escrow plan for evaluation assets + restricted test cases

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with our expectations. Hightower Legal will review the preview DocuSign and the redline doc (legal@hightower.ai). We’d like the redacted package delivered by Dec 28 so our SREs can run throughput tests the week of Dec 29.

We’re OK with Redwood-managed KMS for the evaluation period provided the audit CSV is delivered and the presigned links are single-use per email. Please proceed with DocuSign and flag any items that require additional commercial approval on your side.

I’ll loop in legal on a separate thread for final sign-off but consider this a verbal go-ahead for the MAP timeline.

Best,
Marta
Director of Data Platforms, Hightower Analytics

Attachments referenced (placeholders):
- eval-manifest-v1.csv (counts + file list)
- MAP-milestones.pdf (timeline & gating)
- redlines_hightower_v1.docx (legal redlines)
